repository_card.frontier: The inspected main records finite-lattice area laws, an open hRpoly source programme and an open physical Wilson reflection/transfer bridge. Its continuum limit remains open.
repository_card.bridge_hypothesis: Prioritize edge gauge coordinates and physical reflection, then test uniform integrability tools against the actual raw activity. Dictionary: particle-number bounds -> candidate volume budget; tree reduction -> exact finite lattice coordinates. Neither supplies target-localized RG decay or hRpoly.
repository_card.next_finite_task: Extract three separate checklists: tree-coordinate inverse and Haar identity; reflection compatibility for the physical cylinder; parameter dependence of a candidate exponential-moment estimate. Route each obligation to its satellite before changing a terminal hypothesis.
repository_card.falsifier: Reject any route that loses target support, hides volume/scale dependence, substitutes a real-time dissipative gap, or cites a general convergence theorem without its source estimate.
repository_card.proposal_status: speculative; not executed or formally verified

sources.title: Efficient Quantum Simulations of Yang-Mills theory with Maximal-tree Gauge
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.review_depth: v1: abstract and maximal-tree gauge construction
sources.source_claim: Li and collaborators use maximal-tree gauge and field-amplitude digitization to obtain polynomial resource bounds for Hamiltonian Yang-Mills simulation through QSVT.
sources.limits: Hamiltonian simulation complexity is distinct from an exact Haar edge-coordinate equivalence, Euclidean reflection positivity, and a continuum mass gap. First posted 27 August; a September news mention is not a new submission.

sources.title: Non-Abelian string melting and thermalization in an open lattice gauge theory
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.review_depth: v1: model, thermalization discussion and strong-dephasing reduction
sources.source_claim: A tensor-network study couples 1+1D SU(2) gauge theory with matter to a gauge-preserving Lindblad bath. It finds nonmonotonic relaxation and derives an exclusion-process description in a strong-dephasing limit.
sources.limits: This is an open-system finite/truncated lattice setting, not pure 4D Euclidean Yang-Mills. A Liouvillian relaxation rate is not automatically a Hamiltonian gap, and the strong-dephasing expansion has its own regime.

sources.title: Uniform Partition-Function Estimates for Coulomb Modulated Energy at All Positive Temperatures
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.source_claim: Wang and Zhao report particle-number-uniform partition-function bounds for centered Coulomb-type modulated energies in a locally square-integrable regime, with a second-chaos Fredholm-determinant limit.
sources.limits: Positive-real-parameter integrability does not establish complex zero-freeness. Particle-number uniformity is not automatically RG-scale, support or volume uniformity in the Yang-Mills activity norm. First posted 1 September.

sources.title: The prescribed Hermitian-Yang-Mills flow I
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.source_claim: The prescribed Hermitian-Yang-Mills flow paper establishes convergence for a class of prescribed Hermitian tensors; a parabolic comparison principle supplies the uniform C0 estimate.
sources.limits: This is a flow of Hermitian metrics on holomorphic bundles, not Wilson lattice gradient flow. Read the precise tensor and manifold assumptions before importing a comparison principle. Version 2 is dated 5 September; version 1 is from June.

sources.title: On Quasiparticles within the Refined Gribov-Zwanziger Model
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.source_claim: The refined Gribov-Zwanziger effective model is reexamined through PT symmetry, with a proposed interpretation of quadratic excitations in the real-mass-pole case.
sources.limits: An effective gauge-fixed propagator and real poles do not establish reflection positivity for gauge-invariant Wilson observables, OS reconstruction, or a physical mass gap.
